issues.legal_issue: A newly conferred power of revision applies to a pending eviction proceeding when the appellate order is made after the amendment creating that power has taken effect.
material_facts: The landlord brought an eviction proceeding before the amendment, and the proceeding remained pending when the amendment took effect.
The amendment created a power for the High Court to examine orders made under the rent law.
The appellate authority made its decision after the amendment took effect.
issues.conclusion: The revision application was competent, and the High Court had jurisdiction to hear it; finality attached to the appellate decision only when that decision was made, by which time the amendment was in force.
issues.legal_principle: Under Indira Sohanlal v. Custodian of Evacuee Property, Delhi, finality prescribed for a decision arises when the decision is actually made, not earlier. The Court followed that principle and referred to Delhi Cloth and General Mills Co. Ltd. v. Income-tax Commissioner, Colonial Sugar Refining Co. Ltd. v. Irving, and Garikapatti Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhury.

predicates.rent_control_ejectment_case: A landlord sought to evict a tenant in a proceeding governed by rent-control law.
predicates.proceeding_pending_when_review_power_cre: The eviction proceeding was still pending when a legislative change created a new power to review orders.
predicates.appellate_order_after_review_power_creat: The appellate authority made its order after the new review power took effect.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding remains pending as a new review power takes effect and the appellate order is made afterward, a High Court revision under that power is competent.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment that substantively narrows the grounds for eviction does not govern proceedings already pending unless retrospective operation is expressly provided or necessarily implied.
material_facts: The landlord applied for eviction on the ground that the shop was required for reconstruction before the amendment took effect.
The amendment substantially narrowed the circumstances in which a landlord could recover possession for building work.
The proceeding was pending when the amendment took effect, and the amendment contained no express direction that the changed eviction ground applied retrospectively.
issues.conclusion: The amended eviction ground did not apply to the pending proceeding, which remained governed by the earlier provision.
issues.legal_principle: An amendment affecting substantive rights operates prospectively unless retrospective operation is expressly stated or follows by necessary implication. The Court held that the amendment to s. 13(3)(a)(iii) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, was substantive, found no express or necessarily implied retrospective operation, and approved Ram Parshad Halwai, Ludhiana v. Mukhtiar Chand. The Act’s beneficial purpose for tenants did not determine the question of retrospectivity.

rule.if: rent_control_ejectment_case and eviction_application_preceded_substantive_change and proceeding_pending_when_change_took_effect and not express_retroactivity and not necessary_retroactivity

predicates.rent_control_ejectment_case: A landlord sought to evict a tenant in a proceeding governed by rent-control law.
predicates.eviction_application_preceded_substantiv: The landlord applied for eviction before a legislative change altered the substantive grounds for recovering possession.
predicates.proceeding_pending_when_change_took_effe: The eviction proceeding remained pending when the substantive change took effect.
predicates.express_retroactivity: The legislative change expressly made the altered eviction ground applicable to earlier proceedings.
predicates.necessary_retroactivity: Applying the altered eviction ground to earlier proceedings was necessary for the change to operate.

issues.definition: A pending rent-control eviction proceeding remains governed by the earlier eviction ground when the application preceded a substantive change and the change is neither expressly nor necessarily retrospective.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising statutory revision power to examine the legality or propriety of an order may reassess a finding on a landlord’s asserted need for reconstruction and uphold that need when the evidence supports it.
material_facts: The rent controller and appellate authority rejected the landlord’s reconstruction claim, applying considerations associated with the amended eviction ground even though the earlier ground governed the proceeding.
The landlord obtained approval of a reconstruction plan and municipal sanction soon after purchasing the shop.
The High Court found no legal evidence supporting the lower authorities’ conclusion that the reconstruction claim was not bona fide and allowed the revision.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was entitled to examine the propriety of the lower authorities’ finding, and its conclusion that the landlord’s reconstruction claim was bona fide was neither irregular nor improper.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(5) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, authorized the High Court to examine the legality or propriety of an order and conferred wider power than s. 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Under the applicable earlier s. 13(3)(a)(iii), the Court accepted that the landlord’s requirement had to be bona fide; the evidence of prompt planning and municipal approval supported the High Court’s finding.

rule.if: rent_control_ejectment_case and statutory_revision_authorizes_legality_or_propriety_review and lower_finding_used_inapplicable_eviction_test and landlord_obtained_reconstruction_approval and evidence_supports_bona_fide_need

predicates.rent_control_ejectment_case: A landlord sought to evict a tenant in a proceeding governed by rent-control law.
predicates.statutory_revision_authorizes_legality_o: The governing review provision authorized the High Court to examine the legality or propriety of orders made in the proceeding.
predicates.lower_finding_used_inapplicable_eviction: The lower authorities assessed the landlord’s claim using a test that did not govern the pending proceeding.
predicates.landlord_obtained_reconstruction_approva: The landlord obtained approval for a plan to reconstruct the building.
predicates.evidence_supports_bona_fide_need: The evidence supported the landlord’s asserted need to reconstruct the building as genuine.

issues.definition: Where statutory revision permits review of legality or propriety, the lower finding used an inapplicable test, and evidence supports a genuine reconstruction need, the High Court may reassess the finding and uphold that need.
